author: blu
body: THERE IS NO EXCEPTION RECORD ON THIS MACHINE, and `ii-fault-report` is what exists instead. Nothing in the address map stores a faulting vector, RIP or RSP; the only cells that ever hold a RIP are the watchdog's, and the timer ISR writes them when neither the heap pointer nor the saved RIP has moved since the last tick. So a slot is a sample of a system that had stopped advancing, which is close to the question an operator asks after a hang and is NOT the same as a trap frame. Naming it "the last fault" would be inventing a record the machine does not keep.

author: blu
body: THE TYPE IS NAMED ONLY WHERE THE NAME IS CERTAIN. An unknown type is reported as its number rather than guessed at, for the same reason the fact log reports a raw kind: an inspector that renames the thing it is inspecting is worth less than no inspector.

author: blu
body: A vector outside the table is REFUSED and names the value it rejected. `ii-entry-addr` of 300 is an address inside whatever follows the table, and it would decode into a confident, entirely fictional gate.

author: blu
body: Both cells are zeroed before `sti` and moved only by an ISR, so zero means the handler has never run rather than that the count wrapped. Naming the two states apart is the whole value of the command: a tick count of zero on a running system says the timer never armed, and that reads identically to a slow boot if the line just prints a number.

author: blu
body: Newest first. The slot is the head minus one minus the row, and the whole table is offset by a multiple of the slot count before the modulo so the arithmetic never reaches a negative index.

author: blu
body: A ring with fewer samples than slots must not print the slots it has not written yet: `alloc-bytes` does not zero, and neither did anything else pass over this band, so an unwritten slot holds whatever the firmware left and would render as a plausible RIP.

author: blu
body: The newest slot on its own, for the console views that want a RIP and an RSP rather than a table. `ii-stall-sampled` GUARDS BOTH READERS and is not decoration: with an empty ring the newest-slot arithmetic lands on slot three, which has never been written, so an unguarded read answers whatever the firmware left there. That is precisely the failure these two functions were written to repair, and repeating it one address to the left would not be an improvement.
